name: Positive Enlarged Rows Need Not Peel to the Old Contraction
statement: There is a cornerless $3348$-concept ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness of the form $V(H,D)$, with positive enlarged row $D$ and old contraction $C\subsetneq D$, such that every corner of $D$ lies in $C$. Hence no relative peeling $D\searrow C$ can begin. The output cannot be obtained from the ordinary block replacement of $H$ by a nonempty sequence of ample one-concept additions.
proof: Use the certified $42/22$ nested pair and its rectangular obstruction. Products make $D=P'\times P$ positive and give $\operatorname{Cor}(D)\subseteq P'\times O\subseteq C$, excluding a first relative deletion. The one-row theorem gives forbiddenness. The old block replacement is cornerless and every old vertex has a block neighbour. Enlarging the $01$ row cannot create an old corner because the necessary block mate of each new row word is absent; a new word could be a corner only in $\operatorname{Cor}(D)\setminus C$, which is empty. A nonempty one-concept extension sequence would leave its last word as a corner, a contradiction.
